'''Auktyon''' ({{langx|ru|АукцЫон}}, {{IPA|ru|ɐʊktsɨˈon|pron}}. Auktsyon) is a  [[Soviet]] and Russian [[Avantrock|avant-garde]] rock band from [[Saint Petersburg]].

The band was founded by {{ill|Leonid Fyodorov (musician)|lt=Leonid Fyodorov|ru|Фёдоров, Леонид Валентинович}} in 1978. Though they originally played [[post-punk]] and [[New wave music|new wave]], the group came to be influenced by European and Central Asian folk music, [[avant-garde jazz]], the poetry of Russian futurist [[Velimir Khlebnikov]], and aspects of Russian [[high culture]] and literature.

Auktyon was particularly popular from 1987 through 1995, but became less active in the late 1990s when Fyodorov began to produce records for [[Leningrad (band)|Leningrad]]. The group continues to play together and to release new albums. They toured the United States in 2006 in support of their first US release, the album ''Pioneer''. The group returned to the US in 2008 when they released the album ''Girls Sing.'' Between 2011 and 2020, Auktyon released several albums, while continuing to tour. The group also contributed to film projects, including the soundtrack for [[Aleksei Balabanov|Aleksei Balabanov's]] ''[[Me Too (2012 film)|Me Too]]'' (2012), and was featured in the 2014 documentary ''Eshche''. Their twelfth studio album, ''Sokrovishche'', was released in 2025.

== History ==

=== Early period ===

In the autumn of 1978, Leonid Fyodorov formed a band with his classmates. They started as a trio: Leonid Fyodorov (guitar), Dmitry Zaychenko (bass), and Alexey Vikhrev (drums). Two years later, two more of Fyodorov's school friends joined the group: Mikhail Makov (guitar, vocals) and Viktor Bondarik (bass), while Zaychenko switched to the organ. Around the same time, Sergey "Skvo" Skvortsov joined the group as a sound engineer and lighting technician.<ref name="Burlaka_2007">{{cite book |last=Burlaka |first=Andrey |title=Рок-энциклопедия: Популярная музыка в Ленинграде-Петербурге, 1965–2005 |trans-title=Rock Encyclopedia: Popular Music in Leningrad–Saint Petersburg, 1965–2005 |volume=1 |publisher=Амфора |year=2007 |isbn=978-5-367-00362-8 |language=ru}}</ref><ref name="Beumers_2005">{{cite book |last=Beumers |first=Birgit |title=Pop Culture Russia! |year=2005 |location=Santa Barbara |publisher=[[ABC-CLIO]] |isbn=1-85109-459-8}}</ref> The band began performing at dances in 1981, changing its name from Blue Boys to Paragraph and subsequently to Phaeton.<ref name="Margolis_2010">{{cite book |last=Margolis |first=Mikhail |title=АукцЫон: Книга учета жизни |trans-title=Auktyon: Book of Life |year=2010 |url=https://prochtenie.ru/fragments/15983 |publisher=Амфора |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241107095538/https://prochtenie.ru/fragments/15983 |archive-date=November 7, 2024 |access-date=November 6, 2026 |isbn=978-5-367-01615-4 |via=Прочтение}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Menshenina |first=Elena |date=13 March 2014 |title=Рокеры-романтики. Несколько фактов из истории «АукцЫона» |url=https://aif.ru/rm/rmfacts/1124044 |trans-title=Rock romantics: Some facts from the history of Auktyon |work=Аргументы и Факты |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140313230703/https://aif.ru/rm/rmfacts/1124044 |archive-date=March 13, 2014 |access-date=November 6, 2026}}</ref>

Around 1979, Oleg Garkusha became acquainted with Fyodorov. The group initially rehearsed in Fyodorov's apartment, where he composed the music using texts found in various books and magazines. Garkusha subsequently contributed his poetry to the band's repertoire. The group subsequently moved from Fyodorov's apartment to its first dedicated rehearsal space, the Leningradets youth club in Leningrad.<ref name="Margolis_2010" /><ref name="Spbdnevnik_2021">{{cite web |title=Олег Гаркуша: Перед вступлением в рок-клуб не спали всю ночь |url=https://special.spbdnevnik.ru/garkusha |trans-title=Oleg Garkusha: We stayed up all night before joining the rock club |website=Петербургский дневник |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210613163721/https://special.spbdnevnik.ru/garkusha |archive-date=June 13, 2021 |access-date=November 6, 2026}}</ref> At that time, the ensemble consisted of Alexey Vittel, Dmitry Zaychenko, Alexander Pompeyev (keyboards), Viktor Bondarik, and Mikhail Makov.<ref name="Margolis_2010" />

In 1980, Fyodorov met Dmitry Ozersky. Initially, Ozersky did not play any instruments and served solely as a lyricist. Following Fyodorov's advice, he began learning to play the keyboards—starting at a music school, though he later left the school and continued his studies independently.<ref name="Margolis_2010" /> 

By the spring of 1981, the lineup of Phaeton included: Leonid Fyodorov, Viktor Bondarik, Sergey Skvortsov, Dmitry Ozersky (keyboards), Sergey Melnik (guitar), and Yevgeny Chumichev (drums), as well as Oleg Garkusha—who, depending on the circumstances, served as a sound engineer, manager, and roadie, while also providing sound effects on stage.<ref name="Burlaka_2007" />

=== Joining the Leningrad Rock Club ===

In 1983, the band's bassist, Viktor Bondarik, began his military service and was replaced by Sergey Gubenko. Unsure of his own vocal abilities, Fyodorov invited Valery Nedomovny to serve as lead singer. Oleg Garkusha introduced the band—which was still called Phaeton at the time—to the group [[Aquarium (band)|Aquarium]]. Mikhail Feinstein, who was a member of Aquarium back then, advised them to join the newly founded [[Leningrad Rock Club]].<ref name="Burlaka_2007" />

On May 14, 1983, the band was admitted to the Rock Club as a candidate member and learned the date for their debut concert (scheduled for late autumn 1983). The lineup shifted: Nedomovny (vocals) and Melnik (guitar) left the band and were replaced by guitarist and singer Sergey Lobachev.<ref name="Burlaka_2007" /> In preparation for their first major performance, the band members chose a new name while browsing through a dictionary, but did not get beyond the letter "A"<ref>{{cite web |last=Курий |first=Сергей |date=November 9, 2016 |title=Происхождение названия группы АУКЦЫОН, ее символики и имиджа |url=https://www.kursivom.ru/происхождение-названия-аукцыон/ |trans-title=The Origin of the Band's Name AUKTSION, Its Symbolism, and Image |website=КУР.С.ИВ.ом |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261107073517/https://www.kursivom.ru/%D0%BF%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%85%D0%BE%D0%B6%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%B5-%D0%BD%D0%B0%D0%B7%D0%B2%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%8F-%D0%B0%D1%83%D0%BA%D1%86%D1%8B%D0%BE%D0%BD/ |archive-date=November 7, 2026 |access-date=November 7, 2026}}</ref> before settling on "Auktyon".<ref name="Margolis_2010" /><ref name="OmskZdes_2023">{{cite web |date=July 6, 2023 |title=#МагияВинила: питерский "АукцЫон", или Дом на колёсах |url=https://omskzdes.ru/culture/82011.html |trans-title=#TheMagicOfVinyl: St. Petersburg's "Auktsyon", or A House on Wheels |website=Омск Здесь |language=ru |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312134116/https://omskzdes.ru/culture/82011.html |archive-date=March 12, 2025 |access-date=November 7, 2026}}</ref>

The debut concert took place on November 18, 1983<ref name="Burlaka_2007" /> and, according to the band members, did not go particularly well. Following the concert, Lobachev, Gubenko, and Chumichev left the group.<ref name="Burlaka_2007" /><ref name="Margolis_2010" /><ref name="Angliya">{{cite interview |last=Garkusha |first=Oleg |interviewer-last=Mayorova |interviewer-first=Elena |title=Олег Гаркуша: «Успех — это дело случая» |url=https://angliya.com/publication/oleg-garkusha-uspeh-eto-delo-sluchaya/ |trans-title=Oleg Garkusha: "Success is a matter of chance" |publisher=Angliya |location=London |language=ru |date=October 25, 2018 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250522141634/https://angliya.com/publication/oleg-garkusha-uspeh-eto-delo-sluchaya/ |archive-date=May 22, 2025 |access-date=November 7, 2026}}</ref> The band experienced a series of other setbacks, including losing access to its rehearsal space and the theft of its equipment.<ref name="Angliya" /> Although the band had officially joined the Rock Club, a two-year period of inactivity followed (lasting until 1985). During this time, they were working on new material and about ten different drummers, guitarists, bassists, and singers passed through Auktyon, though none managed to establish a permanent place in the band.<ref name="OmskZdes_2023" /><ref name="Angliya" />

=== 1985–1986. Reunion and ''Come Back to Sorrento'' ===

By early 1985, following a hiatus, Auktyon resumed active rehearsals. The band's lineup stabilized: Bondarik (who had returned from military service) on bass, Ozersky on keyboards, Igor Cheridnik on drums, and Nikolai Fedorovich on alto saxophone. The band began working on a new program of songs. Fedorov, feeling insecure about his own singing, invited vocalist Sergey Rogozhin (whom Ozersky had "discovered") to join the band:

{{Quote box
 | quote      = <small>I walked into the Metallistov Palace of Culture and saw an empty hall with a panel of judges <…> It was absolute madness on stage: Garkusha was darting around with his bizarre, jerky movements, and Lenya Fedorov was singing—at the time, he couldn't seem to pronounce about 32 letters of the alphabet! <…> The judges watched for a while and finally delivered their verdict: 'Either take your lead singer to a speech therapist, or replace him, don't you think?' The members of Auktyon stood there, looking bewildered. They turned to the judges and declared, 'We do have a lead singer. He's right there—sitting in the audience.' Lenya was pointing at me—even though he had never seen or heard me before that moment! It was a complete gamble. And I didn't know a single Auktyon song! <…> As I walked toward the stage, I frantically wondered, 'What on earth am I going to sing?' Then, it hit me. Back in [[Zaporizhzhia]], where I grew up, a Hungarian band called Piramis had come to perform <…> There was one [[Power ballad|rock ballad]] of theirs that I had absolutely loved. That's the one I decided to perform. So, I began to sing it—[[a cappella]]—in Hungarian!… When I finished, a few scattered claps rang out behind me. It was the members of Auktyon themselves, applauding. Someone from the audience remarked: 'Well, it turns out you have an excellent lead singer—every word can be heard! Why didn't you mention him before?'</small>
 | source     = Sergey Rogozhin, ''Tabloid''<ref name="Tabloid_2014">{{cite magazine |date=July 12, 2014 |last=Sychev |first=Sergey |title=Radiola. God 1986 |url=http://tabloid.net.ru/radiola-god-1986/ |magazine=Tabloid |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210615120908/http://tabloid.net.ru/radiola-god-1986/ |archive-date=June 15, 2021 |access-date=November 7, 2026}}</ref>
 | width      = 100%
 | align      = right
 | bgcolor    = #f9f9f9
}}

Artist Kirill Miller also joined the group, taking charge of stage design and the musicians' visual style.<ref name="Margolis_2010" /> In May 1986, the band gave a successful performance at the 4th Leningrad Rock Festival with a lineup consisting of Leonid Fedorov (guitar, vocals), Oleg Garkusha (dancing, vocals), Sergey Rogozhin (vocals), Viktor Bondarik (bass), Dmitry Ozersky (keyboards, vocals), Nikolai Rubanov (saxophones, flutes), Nikolai Fedorovich (saxophone), and Igor Cheridnik (drums). Rogozhin received an award for best vocals, while Oleg Garkusha was recognized for his stage presence.<ref name="Auktyon.com_History_2001">{{cite web |title=History |url=http://www.auktyon.com/history.html |website=Auktyon.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010123132000/http://www.auktyon.com/history.html |archive-date=January 23, 2001 |access-date=November 7, 2026}}</ref> At the invitation of journalist and promoter Andrei Kolomoisky, the group also played two concerts at the ''Sever'' club in the city of [[Vyborg]].

Upon their return, the band began performing periodically at various community centers. One of these shows was recorded by Sergey Firsov and subsequently circulated as a [[cassette tape]] titled ''Rio-de-Shushary''. The recording is considered a rarity though in 2014, it was reissued on [[Compact disc|CD]] as part of the album ''{{ill|D'observer|ru|Д’обсервер}}''.

Fedorov, eager to capture their successful set on tape, led the group through various recording sessions to produce the album ''{{ill|Vernis v Sorrento|ru|Вернись в Сорренто (альбом)}}'' (''Return to Sorrento''), which was not officially released until several years later.<ref name="Margolis_2010" />

=== 1987: A New Program and Lineup Changes ===

By 1987, Auktyon had already become a popular band. They made a cameo appearance in the film ''{{ill|The Burglar (1987 film)|lt=The Burglar|ru|Взломщик (фильм, 1987)}}'', with Oleg Garkusha playing a supporting role as a friend of the protagonist.

Fedorov and Ozersky prepared a new set of songs titled ''Everything Is Calm in Baghdad'' (''{{ill|V Bagdade vse spokoyno|ru|В Багдаде всё спокойно (альбом)}}''). Meanwhile, saxophonist Nikolai Fedorovich left the band. According to Ozersky, the material was inspired by the works of [[E.T.A. Hoffmann]], envisioned as a kind of magical land: "We imagined this 'dreamland' as something like the United Arab Emirates—perhaps one where the oil had run out, or something similar. In essence, these were purely speculative attempts to transpose Hoffmann's world into our own contemporary reality."

The program was unveiled in June 1987 at the 5th Leningrad Rock Festival. During the performance, the band incorporated Eastern-inspired motifs into their stage design and costumes. The new songs, however, received a lukewarm response from both the audience and critics. To make matters worse, Rogozhin—the vocalist for whom the program had been specifically tailored—announced his departure from Auktyon to join the band {{ill|Forum (band)|lt=Forum|ru|Форум (группа)}}. Guitarist Igor Skaldin joined briefly, followed by Dmitry Matkovsky, and the lineup was further bolstered by the addition of percussionist Pavel Litvinov. Dancer {{ill|Vladimir Vesyolkin|ru|Весёлкин, Владимир Олегович}} also joined the group. Ultimately, the band set aside the "Everything Is Calm in Baghdad" program and began working on new material.<ref name="Burlaka_2007" />

=== 1988: ''How I Became a Traitor'' ===

Following an active touring schedule in 1987, violinist and vocalist {{ill|Yevgeny Dyatlov|ru|Дятлов, Евгений Валерьевич}} joined the band. In May 1988, the group began recording the album ''How I Became a Traitor'' (''{{ill|Kak ya stal predatelem|ru|Как я стал предателем}}''), marking their first experience working in a professional studio environment. The album's title was taken from a line in a poem by Oleg Garkusha, "That's How I Became a Traitor"—a phrase inspired by a television program about a former [[TASS]] employee who had become a spy. This line was later incorporated into the lyrics of the song "New Year's Song" ("Novogodnyaya pesnya"), which appears on the album. For reasons unknown, Kirill Miller, who designed the album artwork, rendered the title as ''How I Became a Traitor'' (''Kak ya stal predatelem'').<ref name="Kushnir_1999">{{cite book |last=Semelyak |first=Max |chapter=Аукцыон — Как я стал предателем |trans-chapter=Auktyon — How I Became a Traitor |title=100 Magnitoalbomov Sovetskogo Roka |trans-title=100 Cassette Albums of Soviet Rock |editor-last=Kushnir |editor-first=Alexander |year=1999 |pages=144-145 |url=http://www.rockanet.ru/100/89.phtml |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110831110138/http://www.rockanet.ru/100/89.phtml |archive-date=August 31, 2011 |via=RockaNet.ru |language=ru}}</ref> "We moved away from songs that came, so to speak, from the 'head'—from a purely intellectual approach—toward somewhat more metaphysical material, attempting to push beyond the boundaries we had set for ourselves. While working on this material, I felt a sense of personal growth; I realized I was maturing and beginning to think differently than I had before", noted Dmitry Ozersky. On June 5, 1988, the band presented this material at the 6th Leningrad Rock Festival. In his diary, Vladimir Veselkin described the concert: "It was a triumph for the band. Everything was being filmed."<ref>{{cite web |last=Veselkin |first=Vladimir |title=Дневник. 1988 год |url=https://www.auctyon.ru/article/dnev88.html |trans-title=Diary. 1988 |website=Auktyon.ru |language=ru |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927042748/http://www.auctyon.ru/article/dnev88.html |archive-date=September 27, 2011 |access-date=April 21, 2011}}</ref> Dissatisfied with what he perceived as a secondary role within the group, Dyatlov announced his departure.

Throughout the summer and autumn of 1988, the band toured extensively across the [[USSR]]. Meanwhile, drummer Igor Cheridnik left to join the band {{ill|Igry|ru|Игры (группа)}}, prompting an urgent search for a replacement. After considering several other candidates, the position was filled by Boris Shaveynikov, who joined the band just before their tour of the [[Russian Far East|Far East]]. It is to Boris that the band owes its name; he wrote it with a [[Eye dialect|deliberate misspelling]]—"AuktsYon" (АукцЫон). The band liked the name, and it stuck. At the end of 1988, the group took part in a memorial concert for [[Alexander Bashlachev]] at the [[Luzhniki Sports Palace]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Smirnov |first=Ilya |title=Мемориал Александра Башлачёва в Лужниках, 20.11.1988 |trans-title=Alexander Bashlachev Memorial in Luzhniki, November 20, 1988 |magazine=[[:ru:Сельская молодёжь|Сельская молодёжь]] |issue=11 |page=38 |date=1989 |language=ru |via=Gruppakino |url=https://gruppakino.narod.ru/mitn.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070304011833/https://gruppakino.narod.ru/mitn.html |archive-date=March 4, 2007 |access-date=November 10, 2026}}</ref>

Late that year, the December issue of ''{{ill|Aurora (Russian magazine)|lt=Aurora|ru|Аврора (журнал, Санкт-Петербург)}}'' magazine published a list of the best Soviet rock albums, compiled over the previous six months based on the opinions of critics and readers. Not a single Auktyon record appeared on the 25-album list. Nevertheless, the band's recordings found a certain level of success in the West, and in 1989, the group embarked on its first tour abroad.<ref>{{cite web |last=Boyarinov |first=Denis |date=October 16, 2015 |title=Tantsor riska |url=https://takiedela.ru/2015/10/veselkin/ |trans-title=Dancer of Risk |website=Takiye Dela |language=ru |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312104941/https://takiedela.ru/2015/10/veselkin/ |archive-date=March 12, 2025 |access-date=March 12, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Khomyakova |first=Natasha |date=January 31, 2022 |title=Artefakty shou-biznesa 1980-kh na vystavke «Viktor Tsoy. Put' geroya» |url=https://i-m-i.ru/post/tsoi-exhibition |trans-title=Show Business Artifacts of the 1980s at the Exhibition "Viktor Tsoi: The Hero's Journey" |work=[[:ru:Институт музыкальных инициатив|IMI Journal]] |publisher=Institute of Music Initiatives (IMI) |language=ru |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312111214/https://i-m-i.ru/post/tsoi-exhibition |archive-date=March 12, 2025 |access-date=March 12, 2025}}</ref>

=== 1989: Tours Abroad ===

On February 1, 1989, Auktyon arrived in Berlin, accompanied by the bands [[Zvuki Mu]] and [[Va-Bank]], as well as singer Ekaterina Surzhikova. Two months later, the band toured France alongside [[Kino (band)|Kino]] and Zvuki Mu to promote the CD ''How I Became a Traitor'' (''Kak ya stal predatelem''), which had been released there. It was also in France that the band had a momentous encounter with [[Alexei Khvostenko]]—a figure who would later play a significant role in both the band's own work and the solo projects of Leonid Fyodorov. These trips to France were also linked to a well-known scandal involving the band. During a festival in [[Le Bourget]], Vladimir Veselkin performed a mock striptease while the song "Nepman" was playing, ending up in nothing but flesh-colored undergarments. This incident drew negative coverage in the Soviet newspapers ''[[Sovetskaya Kultura]]'' and ''[[Komsomolskaya Pravda]]''. ''Komsomolskaya Pravda'' published an article titled "Pop Music? Showing off real skill proved difficult—so they showed off bad taste instead", accusing the band of vulgarity and poor taste.<ref>{{cite news |last=Dolgopolov |first=Nikolai |date=April 12, 1989 |title=ЗВУКИ МУ, КИНО, АУКЦЫОН |url=http://www.nneformat.ru/archive/?id=4208 |trans-title=Sounds of Mu, Kino, Auktyon |newspaper=[[Komsomolskaya Pravda]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022164251/http://www.nneformat.ru/archive/?id=4208 |archive-date=October 22, 2012 |access-date=November 8, 2026 |via=Наш НеФормат}}</ref> Vladimir Veselkin gathered signatures from prominent figures in the Leningrad cultural scene and succeeded in getting an "Open Letter from the Band Auktyon" published in the May 12, 1989, issue of ''Sovetskaya Kultura''.<ref name="Margolis_2010" /> ''Komsomolskaya Pravda'' offered no response. Later, Veselkin repeated the act during the television program ''{{ill|Musical Ring|ru|Музыкальный ринг}}''. The performance was poorly received, prompting a comment from the audience: "Your deliberately degenerate performance style serves to discredit Soviet rock".<ref name="Margolis_2010" /><ref>{{cite interview |last=Veselkin |first=Vladimir |interviewer= |url=http://www.bostontea.narod.ru/veselkin.html |title=Interview |work=Boston Tea Party |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130521183539/http://www.bostontea.narod.ru/veselkin.html |archive-date=May 21, 2013 |access-date=November 8, 2026 |via=Narod}}</ref> That summer, the band recorded the album ''Everything Is Calm in Baghdad'' at the Leningrad Recording Studio. On the night of June 11–12, 1989, Auktyon closed out the final (seventh) Leningrad Rock Festival. During rehearsals that year, the band was already actively playing the tracks "Airplane", "Pioneer", "Love", and "Tattletale"—songs that would soon make up their next album.

=== 1990–1991: ''Zhopa'' and ''Bodun'' ===

By 1990, the band was actively working on new material. A friendship developed between bassist Viktor Bondarik and drummer Boris Shaveynikov, which helped strengthen the band's rhythm section. Fyodorov arranged for recording sessions at [[Stas Namin]]'s studio, where the album ''[[Zhopa]]'' (''Ass'') was recorded during the winter. The vinyl release featured a truncated version of the album, and for censorship reasons, the title was changed to ''Duplo'' ("Hollow/Cavity"). Also in 1990, the record ''V Bagdade vsyo spokoyno'' (''All Is Quiet in Baghdad'')—recorded back in 1989—was released by the Melodiya label. In May and June, the band took part in the ''Rock of Clean Water'' (''Rok chistoy vody'') festival.

In 1991, the band recorded the album ''{{ill|Bodun|ru|Бодун}}'' (''Hangover''). Its cover art was the last one designed by Miller. The song "Stolby" ("Pillars") was omitted from the initial release due to profanity in the lyrics. These new albums differed significantly in style from the band's previous work—partly due to the influence of Shaveynikov, whose drumming was "heavier." The material became darker and more [[Musical improvisation|improvisational]]. The band toured extensively in Germany, with the tours organized by a German named Christoph Karsten. Miller and Vesyolkin began to drift away from the band; the group itself had grown weary of Vesyolkin's behavior on stage, as he was prone to heavy alcohol abuse. Oleg Garkusha, who was also struggling with heavy alcohol abuse, began to play an increasingly minor role in the band. In 1992, Vesyolkin left the group to pursue a solo project.

=== Mid-1990s. ''Chainik vina'' (''A Teapot of Wine'') and ''Ptitsa'' (''Bird'') ===

Fedorov had long harbored the idea of ​​recording songs by his friend Alexei Khvostenko. However, Khvostenko lived in France—a country where Auktyon had little time to spare during their tours. In 1992, having finally secured the necessary paperwork, Khvostenko arrived in Russia aboard a plane carrying humanitarian aid. Working at the Titanic studio, the band—joined by Khvostenko—recorded the album ''{{ill|Chainik vina|ru|Чайник вина}}'' in a rather short timeframe. Fedorov would later describe it as one of Auktyon's finest works. During this period, Auktyon began touring Europe more frequently, even purchasing a used bus for the purpose.<ref name="Margolis_2010" />

In 1993, the band began recording the album ''{{ill|Ptitsa (album)|lt=Ptitsa|ru|Птица (альбом)}}'' (''Bird''), which would go on to become one of their most popular releases. This was largely due to the inclusion of the song "[[The Road (Auktyon song)|The Road]]" on the soundtrack for Alexei Balabanov's highly successful film ''[[Brother 2]]'' (''Brat-2''), released in 2000. The recording process, including rehearsals, took about six months. The title track was composed by Fedorov and Garkusha while they were staying in the countryside during the attempted coup. Relations within the band were strained at the time; according to Fedorov, the group was on the verge of breaking up.<ref>{{cite web |last=Курий |first=Сергей |title="The Птица" (1993) |url=http://www.ytime.com.ua/ru/50/2059 |website=Рок-толкование |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141023022508/http://www.ytime.com.ua/ru/50/2059 |archive-date=October 23, 2014 |access-date=April 21, 2011}}</ref> Nevertheless, the other band members were pleased with the album. While Fedorov considers the individual songs on the record to be among the best he and Ozersky ever wrote, he generally views ''Ptitsa'' as one of the band's failures. 

{{Quote box
 | quote      = While putting ''Chainik vina'' together, I realized that we had recorded what I consider to be a brilliant album." It suddenly dawned on me that you could create amazing things using minimal resources, without having to come up with anything particularly elaborate. ''Ptitsa'' [Bird] was an attempt to record something like that—without Khvost, just with Auktyon. But the attempt failed. We couldn't manage to make a simple record; the arrangements ruined ''Ptitsa''. Our previous albums—''Kak ya stal predatelem'' [How I Became a Traitor], ''Bodun'', and ''Zhopa'' [Ass]—were recorded exactly the way we wanted them to be; they are far more coherent than ''Ptitsa''.
 | source     = Leonid Fyodorov, Margolis (2010)<ref name="Margolis_2010" />
 | width      = 100%
 | align      = right
 | bgcolor    = #f9f9f9
}}

The album was released in two editions, six months apart (a German version and a Russian version).

=== The Second Half of the 1990s ===

[[File:Chlebnikow.jpg|thumb|Auktyon explored the poetry of [[Velimir Khlebnikov]] in collaboration with avant-garde poet [[Alexei Khvostenko]]. Their 1995 album ''Zhilets vershin'' (''Dweller of the Peaks'') combines Khlebnikov's poems, selected and adapted by Khvostenko, with music by the band, creating a new interpretation of the poet's work.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Vatueva |first=Viktoria A. |title=Poetry of Velimir Khlebnikov in the Works of the Band "Auktyon": On the Example of the Album "Zhilets Vershin" |journal=RSUH/RGGU Bulletin. Literary Theory. Linguistics. Cultural Studies |issue=8 |year=2021 |pages=75–85 |doi=10.28995/2686-7249-2021-8-75-85}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Volkov |first=Alexander V. |date=December 22, 2016 |title=Auktyon: Zhilets vershin (1995/2016) |journal=[[InRock]] |issue=77}}</ref>]]

Following the album ''Ptitsa'', the band entered a creative crisis. Fyodorov managed to overcome this after being introduced to the poetry of Velimir Khlebnikov (with the help of Khvostenko). In 1995, the band—together with Khvostenko—recorded an album based on Khlebnikov's poems, titled ''Zhilets vershin'' (''Dweller of the Peaks'').

The band's activity within Russia began to decline, though Auktyon continued to tour Europe (with particularly frequent performances in Germany).<ref name="Burlaka_2007" /> In November 1995, guitarist Dmitry Matkovsky was dismissed from the group. According to Ozersky, the conflict stemmed from both musical differences—Matkovsky favored a more disciplined approach to performance, while saxophonist Rubanov advocated for improvisation—and personal friction. Matkovsky was replaced by tuba player Mikhail Kolovsky. On July 22, 1996, Oleg Garkusha traveled to America to undergo treatment for alcoholism; he stopped drinking thereafter.

In 1997, the albums ''Vernis v Sorrento'' (''Return to Sorrento'') and ''D'observer'' (a recording of a 1986 concert at the [[Pulkovo Observatory]]) were officially released for the first time. That same year, Fyodorov released his debut solo album, the acoustic ''Chetyrespolovinoytonny'' (''Four and a Half Tons'').

Throughout the late 1990s and early 2000s, Leonid Fyodorov focused on solo projects, collaborating with various other musicians, and producing albums for [[Leningrad (band)|Leningrad]].<ref name="Beumers_2005" /> In 1999, the band released two singles: ''{{ill|Zimy ne budet|ru|Зимы не будет (альбом)}}'' (''There Won't Be a Winter''), credited to "Auktyon, Volkov, Kurashov," and ''Nebo napopolam'' (''Sky Split in Half''), a collaboration between the band and [[Leonid Soybelman]].

=== From 2000 to the Present ===

In 2002, the album ''{{ill|Eto Mama|ru|Это мама}}'' (''This Is Mom'') was released—a recording of the band's live set—featuring two new songs, "Yakorya" ("Anchors") and "O Pogode" ("About the Weather"), as well as "Zaveduyushchiy (Koporye)" ("The Manager (Koporye)"), which had previously appeared on Fyodorov's 1997 solo album.<ref>{{cite web |title=«Это мама» |url=https://www.leonidfedorov.ru/emama.htm |website=Leonid Fyodorov official website |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030305192816/https://www.leonidfedorov.ru/emama.htm |archive-date=March 5, 2003 |access-date=November 8, 2026}}</ref> On December 15, 2005, percussionist Pavel Litvinov passed away following a second stroke.

Auktyon toured the United States in 2006<ref name="BostonGlobe_2006">{{cite news |last=Mitter |first=Siddhartha |date=24 March 2006 |title=By way of Russia, art-rock for art's sake |newspaper=[[Boston Globe]] |page=D.1}}</ref><ref name="NYTimes_2005">{{cite news |last=Sisario |first=Ben |date=November 21, 2005 |title=Arts, Briefly |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/11/21/arts/arts-briefly.html |url-access=subscription |newspaper=[[New York Times]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150529191203/https://www.nytimes.com/2005/11/21/arts/arts-briefly.html |archive-date=May 29, 2015 |access-date=November 8, 2026}}</ref> in support of their first US release, the compilation album ''[[Pioneer (Auktyon album)|Pioneer]]''. The next full-length studio album, ''{{ill|Devushki Poyut|ru|Девушки поют}}'' (''Girls Are Singing''), was released in 2007, following a 12-year hiatus.<ref name="NYTimes_2008">{{cite news |last=Sisario |first=Ben |date=24 March 2006 |title=Pop and Rock Listings |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/03/21/arts/music/21pop.html |url-access=subscription |newspaper=[[New York Times]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180106024653/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/03/21/arts/music/21pop.html |archive-date=January 6, 2018 |access-date=November 9, 2026}}</ref> It was recorded in New York at Stratosphere Sound Studios, with contributions from American musicians [[Marc Ribot]], [[John Medeski]], [[Frank London]], and [[Ned Rothenberg]], alongside Russian double bassist Vladimir Volkov.<ref>{{cite magazine |date=October 2006 |title=Рецензия на концерт |trans-title=Concert review |magazine=[[:ru:Fuzz (журнал)|FUZZ]] |volume=10 |issue=157 |language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=«Девушки поют» |url=https://www.leonidfedorov.ru/dp.htm |trans-title=Girls Sing |website=Leonid Fyodorov official website |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250518071621/http://www.leonidfedorov.ru/dp.htm |archive-date=May 18, 2025 |access-date=November 8, 2026}}</ref> In 2008 and 2009,  they toured the US again in support of the album.<ref name="NYTimes_2008" /><ref>{{cite news |last=Vigil |first=Delfin |date=27 March 2008 |title=Auktyon. Eclectic band formed in the former Soviet Union and, 20 years later, strange, loud rock plays a key role in the group's musical stylings |newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |page=G.4}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=18 March 2008 |last=Drozdowski |first=Ted |title=Auktyon - CD Reviews |url=http://thephoenix.com/Boston/music/58205-auktyon-girls-sing/ |newspaper=[[The Phoenix (newspaper)|The Phoenix]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121014185438/http://thephoenix.com/Boston/music/58205-auktyon-girls-sing/ |archive-date=2012-10-14 |access-date=2012-09-19}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Horowitz |first=Steve |date=31 March 2008 |title=Auktyon: Girls Sing |url=https://www.popmatters.com/auktyon-girls-sing-2496176373.html |work=[[PopMatters]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190805154107/https://www.popmatters.com/auktyon-girls-sing-2496176373.html |archive-date=August 5, 2019 |access-date=November 7, 2026}}</ref> 

On October 7, 2011, the band unveiled a new album, ''{{ill|Yula (album)|lt=Yula|ru|Юла (альбом)}}'' (''Spinning Top''), which was recorded without the involvement of foreign guest musicians. The album was produced on a tight schedule—over the course of just 11 days—at the Parametrika studio in Moscow. Vladimir Volkov, who had collaborated with Fyodorov on his solo projects and performed live with Auktyon for several years, took part in the recording.<ref>{{cite web |title=«Аукцыон»: так решил волчок |url=https://rollingstone.ru/articles/Auktsion:-tak-reshil-volchok |trans-title="Auktyon": The Spinning Top Decided So |website=[[Rolling Stone|Rolling Stone Russia]] |language=ru |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111105060215/http://rollingstone.ru/articles/Auktsion:-tak-reshil-volchok |archive-date=November 5, 2011 |access-date=October 8, 2011}}</ref> The album's release was preceded by the launch of the band's official YouTube channel on September 21 of that same year. Trumpeter [[Yuriy Parfyonov]] also participated in the recording; he performed with the band during the album's launch concerts and subsequently became a permanent member of the group. In 2012, the final film by Russian director Aleksei Balabanov, ''[[Me Too (2012 film)|Me Too]]'', was released. Oleg Garkusha played the lead role of "The Musician", Leonid Fyodorov served as the film's composer, and the soundtrack consists entirely of songs by the band and Fyodorov himself.<ref>{{cite news |last=Зинцов |first=Олег |date=December 12, 2012 |title=«Я тоже хочу» Алексея Балабанова: Счастливый конец стал сюжетом |url=https://www.vedomosti.ru/lifestyle/articles/2012/12/12/k_schastyu |trans-title=Alexey Balabanov's ''Me Too'': A Happy Ending Became the Story |newspaper=[[Vedomosti]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230702081022/https://www.vedomosti.ru/lifestyle/articles/2012/12/12/k_schastyu |archive-date=2 July 2023 |access-date=2 July 2023}}</ref>

In 2013, the band celebrated its 30th anniversary with a series of concerts in cities including Moscow, Saint Petersburg, [[Smolensk]], [[Kyiv]], and [[Dnipropetrovsk]]. In December, to mark the 20th anniversary of their album ''Ptitsa'', the group held two exclusive concerts in Moscow and Saint Petersburg, during which they performed every track from that album.

2014 saw the release of the documentary film ''Eshche'' (''More''), directed by [[Dmitry Lavrinenko]]. Filmed over the course of seven years, the project followed the band on tour; the director was present in the studio during the creation of the album ''Yula'', handed the camera to the musicians themselves when they traveled to America to record with Medeski and Ribot, and captured the most intimate moments of the band's performances.

Preview screenings of the film took place in Moscow and Saint Petersburg during the summer. In September 2014, a "film marathon" began, with screenings held in more than 15 cities across Russia and beyond. In several locations—including Moscow, [[Yekaterinburg]], [[Kaluga]], and [[Minsk]]—the band's concerts were timed to coincide with the release of the film. According to director Lavrinenko, a second film is expected to be released soon, focusing on the solo work of Leonid Fedorov and his musical projects with Volkov, [[Sergey Starostin]], and others.

On December 4, 2014—coinciding with the birthday of A. Khvostenko—a posthumous album titled ''Scorpion'' was released, featuring contributions from musicians of the band Auktyon. The album contains 22 tracks in which the author performs his own poetry, as well as fables written in collaboration with [[Anri Volokhonsky]]. The musical arrangements for these poems were created by A. Gerasimov and the members of the band themselves.

Due to various circumstances, work on ''Scorpion'' spanned nearly a decade—from 2004 to 2013—during which time both key figures of the project, Khvostenko and Gerasimov, passed away. Following Khvostenko's death, his daughter, Anna, stepped in to serve as a "critic and advisor" to the musicians during the recording process. The album's title was suggested by Auktyon double bassist Vladimir Volkov, inspired by the poem "Under the Sign of the Scorpion" ("Pod znakom Skorpiona"), which is included in the collection. Much of the recording took place at the apartment of the band's frontman, Leonid Fedorov—who acted as the album's de facto producer—and he subsequently mixed all the tracks in his home studio.

In October 2015, the band worked at the [[Mosfilm]] studio on their next full-length album, ''{{ill|Na solntse|ru|На солнце}}'' (''In the Sun''), which was released in May 2016.<ref>{{cite web |last=Иванова |first=Анастасия |date=October 22, 2015 |title=«Аукцыон» в тонстудии «Мосфильма» |url=https://www.mosfilm.ru/news/index.php?ELEMENT_ID=12164 |trans-title=Auktyon at the Mosfilm Recording Studio |publisher=[[Mosfilm]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116135635/https://www.mosfilm.ru/news/index.php?ELEMENT_ID=12164 |archive-date=January 16, 2018 |access-date=November 4, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=«АУКЦИОН» ВНОВЬ НА «МОСФИЛЬМЕ» |url=https://mosfilm.ru/news/index.php?ELEMENT_ID=12342 |trans-title=Auktyon Once Again at Mosfilm |publisher=[[Mosfilm]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116135246/https://www.mosfilm.ru/news/index.php?ELEMENT_ID=12342 |archive-date=January 16, 2018 |access-date=January 21, 2016}}</ref> In August 2019, it was revealed that Auktyon was recording a new album at the Mosfilm studio, alongside an undisclosed solo project by Leonid Fyodorov.<ref>{{cite web |title=АукцЫон работает над новым студийным альбомом |url=https://reproduktor.net/2019/08/aukcyon-rabotaet-nad-novym-albomom/ |trans-title=Auktyon Is Working on a New Studio Album |website=Reproduktor.net |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200814025225/https://reproduktor.net/2019/08/aukcyon-rabotaet-nad-novym-albomom/ |archive-date=August 14, 2020 |access-date=September 12, 2019}}</ref> The album, titled ''{{ill|Mechty|ru|Мечты (альбом)}}'' (''Dreams''), was released on April 24, 2020. The first single, "Tisha", was released on April 4, followed by the title track, "Mechty", on April 14. Music videos were produced for both songs.<ref>{{cite news |date=April 8, 2020 |title=«Мир изменился, весь мир опустился…» «АукцЫон» выпустил «самоизолированный» клип к новому альбому |url=https://calendar.fontanka.ru/articles/9440/ |trans-title="The World Has Changed, the Whole World Has Fallen..." Auktyon Releases a "Self-Isolated" Music Video for Its New Album |newspaper=[[Fontanka.ru]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200406180413/https://calendar.fontanka.ru/articles/9440/ |archive-date=6 April 2020 |access-date=November 8, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=«АукцЫон» показал танцевальные «Мечты» и анонсировал онлайн-презентацию альбома (Видео) |url=https://www.intermedia.ru/news/346470/ |trans-title=Auktyon Presents the Dance-Oriented "Dreams" and Announces an Online Album Presentation (Video) |agency=[[InterMedia]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200419190236/https://www.intermedia.ru/news/346470/ |archive-date=19 April 2020 |access-date=November 8, 2026}}</ref>

On December 9, 2022, a remastered reissue of the album ''Devushki Poyut'' was released, featuring bonus CD and DVD discs that include improvisational tracks recorded during the studio sessions, as well as a concert film documenting the album's launch at the B1 Maximum venue.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 8, 2022 |title=«АукцЫон» перевыпускает поющих девушек с новым мастерингом и видеобонусами |url=https://www.intermedia.ru/news/375387 |trans-title=Auktyon Reissues ''Devushki Poyut'' with New Mastering and Video Bonus Features |agency=[[InterMedia]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221208214726/https://www.intermedia.ru/news/375387 |archive-date=December 8, 2022 |access-date=November 8, 2026}}</ref>

On November 21, 2025, the band's twelfth studio album, ''{{ill|Sokrovishche|ru|Сокровище (альбом)}}'' (''Treasure''), was released. It consists of eight songs, two of which—"Boroda" ("Beard") and "Musulmanin" ("Muslim")—were accompanied by music videos.<ref>{{cite web |author=Аукцыон |date=November 19, 2025 |title=Аукцыон. Борода. (альбом Сокровище 2025) |trans-title=Auktyon. Beard. (''Sokrovishche'' album, 2025) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s4KcPRQ0YRs |website=[[YouTube]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251121235151/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s4KcPRQ0YRs |archive-date=November 21, 2025 |access-date=November 8, 2026}}</ref> This album also marked the final contribution of Yuri Parfyonov, who passed away in the summer of 2025 but had managed to record his parts before his death. The track "Yurochka" is dedicated to him.

== Artistry ==

=== Musical style ===

Auktyon's music has been described in terms of [[art rock]], [[Avantrock|avant-garde rock]], and [[post-punk]], although critics have frequently emphasized the difficulty of assigning the band to a single genre. A 2006 ''[[Boston Globe]]'' profile described its sound as one that "resists category", while a 2003 article in the Russian newspaper ''[[Moskovsky Komsomolets]]'' stated that "there is no one to compare them to" and identified traces of ska, reggae, and [[nu-jazz]].<ref name="BostonGlobe_2006" /><ref name="MK_2003">{{cite news |last=Legostajew |first=Ilja |date=September 5, 2003 |title=«Аукцыон»: «Не хотим и не умеем быть такими, как все» |url=https://www.mk.ru/editions/daily/article/2003/09/05/127741-auktsyion-he-hotim-i-ne-umeem-byit-takimi-kak-vse.html |trans-title=Auktyon: We do not want to and cannot be like everyone else |newspaper=[[Moskovsky Komsomolets]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110214234417/https://www.mk.ru/editions/daily/article/2003/09/05/127741-auktsyion-he-hotim-i-ne-umeem-byit-takimi-kak-vse.html |archive-date=February 14, 2011 |access-date=November 8, 2026}}</ref> [[Greg Quill]] of the ''[[Toronto Star]]'' similarly characterized the group as "unlike anything we've heard in the West", noting the difficulty of fitting its music into familiar stylistic categories.<ref name="TorontoStar_2006">{{cite news |last=Quill |first=Greg |date=March 23, 2006 |author-link=Greg Quill |title=Passion for Auktyon's pieces: SXSW sensation hard to pin down |url=https://archive.rockpaperscissors.biz/index.cfm/fuseaction/current.articles_detail/project_id/262/article_id/5419.cfm |newspaper=[[Toronto Star]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160614210714/http://archive.rockpaperscissors.biz/index.cfm/fuseaction/current.articles_detail/project_id/262/article_id/5419.cfm |archive-date=June 14, 2016 |access-date=November 8, 2026 |via=Rock Paper Scissors}}</ref> ''[[Afisha]]'' notes that the band has a style for which there is no convincing parallel.<ref name="Afisha_2016">{{cite magazine |last=Sobolev |first=Oleg |date=May 23, 2016 |title=«Кто знает «Аукцыон» — поймет с ходу, что все так, как надо» |url=https://daily.afisha.ru/music/1611-kto-znaet-aukcyon-poymet-s-hodu-chto-vse-tak-kak-nado/amp/ |trans-title="Anyone familiar with Auktyon will immediately recognize that everything is exactly as it should be" |magazine=[[Afisha]] |language=ru |via=Rock Paper Scissors |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261031113641/https://daily.afisha.ru/music/1611-kto-znaet-aukcyon-poymet-s-hodu-chto-vse-tak-kak-nado/amp/ |archive-date=October 31, 2026 |access-date=November 9, 2026}}</ref>

The band's music combines elements of rock with jazz and folk traditions. Contemporary descriptions have associated it with art rock, post-punk, free jazz, [[Latin percussion]] and the sound of military [[marching bands]].<ref name="TorontoStar_2006" /> A 2005 ''[[Willamette Week]]'' article described Auktyon's approach as a form of genre-splicing, identifying influences from Russian folk music, [[avant-jazz]], [[jazz fusion]], and [[psychedelic music]] of the 1960s.<ref name="WillametteWeek_2005">{{cite news |last=Dundas |first=Zach |date=April 26, 2005 |title=Glasnost for Others |url=https://www.wweek.com/portland/article-4348-glasnost-for-others.html |newspaper=[[Willamette Week]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261109025030/https://www.wweek.com/portland/article-4348-glasnost-for-others.html |archive-date=November 9, 2026 |access-date=November 9, 2026}}</ref> A 2008 review in ''[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]'' further identified psychedelic grooves, 1980s pop and contemporary [[World music|ethnic fusion]], particularly Slavic folk music and ska, in the band's sound.<ref name="Inquirer_2008">{{cite news |last=Adler |first=David R. |date=24 March 2008 |title=Auktyon creates own style, aura |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/entertainment/20080324_Auktyon_creates_own_style__aura.html |url-access=subscription |newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261031005246/https://www.inquirer.com/philly/entertainment/20080324_Auktyon_creates_own_style__aura.html |archive-date=October 31, 2026 |access-date=November 8, 2026}}</ref>

Auktyon's arrangements make extensive use of brass and woodwind instruments, including saxophone, bass clarinet and tuba, alongside guitar, keyboards, bass and percussion. The ''[[Boston Globe]]'' noted the prominence of low-register horns and described connections between ska and [[klezmer]] in the band's music.<ref name="BostonGlobe_2006" /> A 1995 review, the German newspaper ''[[die tageszeitung|taz]]'' described the music on the album ''Ptiza'' as a combination of Russian folk harmonies, klezmer rhythms and jazz, with predominantly acoustic instrumentation.<ref name="taz_1995">{{cite news |last=Rademacher |first=Noël |date=October 6, 1995 |title=Hoffnungsvoll hysterisch |url=https://taz.de/Hoffnungsvoll-hysterisch/\!1490038/ |newspaper=[[die tageszeitung]] |language=de |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261109032008/https://taz.de/Hoffnungsvoll-hysterisch/!1490038/ |archive-date=November 9, 2026 |access-date=November 9, 2026}}</ref> Reviewing ''Girls Sing'' in 2008, the ''[[Boston Phoenix]]'' highlighted the album's range from noise-influenced [[cool jazz]] to acoustic [[Romani music#Romani folk music|Gypsy folk]].<ref name="BostonPhoenix_2008">{{cite news |last=Drozdowski |first=Ted |date=March 18, 2008 |title=Auktyon |url=https://thephoenix.com/Boston/music/58205-auktyon-girls-sing/ |newspaper=[[The Boston Phoenix]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080928212234/https://thephoenix.com/Boston/music/58205-auktyon-girls-sing/ |archive-date=September 28, 2008 |access-date=November 9, 2026}}</ref>

The band's musical identity is also associated with theatrical performance. A 1989 ''[[die tageszeitung|taz]]'' concert review described Auktyon's mixture of jazz, new wave, punk, Russian folk music, modern dance and theatre, while noting the group's costumes and stage antics.<ref name="taz_1989">{{cite news |last=Höfer |first=Petra |date=February 9, 1989 |title=Im siebten blockfreien Pophimmel |url=https://taz.de/Im-siebten-blockfreien-Pophimmel/\!1822941/ |newspaper=[[die tageszeitung]] |language=de |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261109032745/https://taz.de/Im-siebten-blockfreien-Pophimmel/!1822941/ |archive-date=November 9, 2026 |access-date=November 9, 2026}}</ref> ''[[Willamette Week]]'' likewise characterized the group by its absurdist stage show and musical intensity, while describing its compositions as unconventional, genre-crossing pieces rather than conventional verse-and-chorus songs.<ref name="WillametteWeek_2005" />

=== Influences ===

Auktyon's musical influences encompassed a wide range of genres, including new wave, post-punk, hard rock, art rock, [[free jazz]] and contemporary classical music. In a 2013 interview with ''[[Colta.ru|Colta]]'', saxophonist Nikolai Rubanov recalled that [[the Cure]] and [[the Police]] had a particularly strong influence on the band during its early years. He also cited free jazz, [[Led Zeppelin]], art rock and contemporary [[chamber music]] among his own musical interests.<ref name="colta_2013">{{cite web |last=Kashapov |first=Radif |date=October 4, 2013 |title=У нас ведь еще и анархия |url=https://www.colta.ru/articles/music_modern/687-u-nas-ved-esche-i-anarhiya |trans-title=There's also anarchy among us |website=[[Colta.ru]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514112751/https://www.colta.ru/articles/music_modern/687-u-nas-ved-esche-i-anarhiya |archive-date=May 14, 2021 |access-date=November 9, 2026}}</ref>

In a 1989 interview with ''[[Die Tageszeitung|taz]]'', guitarist Leonid Fyodorov named the Cure among his favourite bands, while guitarist Dmitry Matkovsky cited [[Talking Heads]]. The interview also noted that the band's members had diverse musical tastes, including Arabic music and hard rock.<ref name="taz_1989" />

In a 1995 interview, Fyodorov identified [[the Beatles]] as his most significant musical influence, describing their impact on rock music as particularly transformative.<ref name="rockarchive_1995">{{cite web |date=1995 |title=АУКЦЫОН: Делать рок-н-ролл слишком просто |url=https://www.rockarchive.ru/text/n-1/265/index.shtml |trans-title=Auktyon: Making rock 'n' roll is too easy |website=Rockarchive.ru |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081023202133/https://www.rockarchive.ru/text/n-1/265/index.shtml |archive-date=October 23, 2008 |access-date=November 9, 2026}}</ref>

In a 2024 interview, vocalist Oleg Garkusha recalled that the band's early musical environment was strongly influenced by British new wave, mentioning Talking Heads, The Police, [[The Clash]], [[Bryan Ferry]], [[Bad Manners]], and [[Madness (band)|Madness]]. He also noted similarities between the early music of Auktyon and the Police.<ref name="snob_2024">{{cite web |last=Spesivtsev |first=Egor |date=May 28, 2024 |title=«У меня нет ни слуха, ни голоса, ничего». Фронтмен «АукцЫона» Олег Гаркуша о любимых пластинках, сольном творчестве и концерте в тюрьме |url=https://snob.ru/music/u-menia-net-ni-slukha-ni-golosa-nichego-frontmen-auktsyona-oleg-garkusha-o-liubimykh-plastinkakh-solnom-tvorchestve-i-kontserte-v-tiurme/ |trans-title=I have neither an ear nor a voice, nothing: Auktyon's frontman Oleg Garkusha on favourite records, solo work and a prison concert |website=[[:ru:Сноб (медиапроект)|Snob]] |language=ru |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240620175706/https://snob.ru/music/u-menia-net-ni-slukha-ni-golosa-nichego-frontmen-auktsyona-oleg-garkusha-o-liubimykh-plastinkakh-solnom-tvorchestve-i-kontserte-v-tiurme/ |archive-date=June 20, 2024 |access-date=November 9, 2026}}</ref>

{{short description|Measure of the air volume added to or removed from a space}}
'''Air changes per hour''', abbreviated '''ACPH''' or '''ACH''', or '''air change rate''' is the ratio of the volumetric airflow rate though a certain time period to the space volume. It is expressed as the number of air changes per hour.
<ref name="CDC-Glossary">{{cite web |title=Appendix A: Glossary of Terms |url=https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/environmental-control/glossary.html |website=Centers for Disease Control and Prevention |date=2024-01-11}}</ref>
Its definition doesn't imply that the entire initial air volume is physically replaced at each nominal air change.

If the air in the space is either uniform or perfectly mixed, air changes per hour is a measure of how many times the air within a defined space is replaced each hour. Perfectly mixed air refers to a theoretical condition where supply air is instantly and uniformly mixed with the air already present in a space, so that conditions such as age of air and concentration of pollutants are spatially uniform.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |year=2002 |title=ASHRAE Standard 129-1997 (RA 2002): Measuring Air-Change Effectiveness |location=Atlanta, GA |publisher=American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers}}</ref>

In many air distribution arrangements, air is neither uniform nor perfectly mixed. The actual percentage of an enclosure's air which is exchanged in a period depends on the airflow efficiency of the enclosure and the methods used to ventilate it. These systems range from a conceptual system of perfect [[Displacement ventilation|displacement]], which removes and replaces all air in a space, to a short circuit flow in which very little of the existing air is replaced.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Fisk |first1=William J. |last2=Faulkner |first2=David |last3=Sullivan |first3=Douglas |last4=Bauman |first4=Fred |date=1997-06-01 |title=Air change effectiveness and pollutant removal efficiency during adverse mixing conditions |journal=Indoor Air |language=English |volume=7 |issue=1 |pages=55–63 |doi=10.1111/j.1600-0668.1997.t01-3-00007.x |osti=803749 |issn=0905-6947|doi-access=free |bibcode=1997InAir...7...55F }}</ref> Concretely, in a perfectly mixed space with a constant ventilation rate, pollutant-free incoming air, no additional pollutant sources and no other removal mechanisms, the concentration of an initially present airborne pollutant decreases exponentially.<ref name="bearg">{{cite book | last = Bearg | first = David W. | title = Indoor Air Quality and HVAC Systems | publisher =  CRC Press | year = 1993 | isbn = 0-87371-574-8 | page = 64 }}</ref> 

The existing relation is : 

<math>{\operatorname{d}\!C\over\operatorname{d}\!t} = - ACH * C
</math>

The solution of this differential equation is: <math>C(t) = C_0 * \exp(- ACH * t)</math> 
<ref name="CDC-Air">{{cite web |title=Appendix B: Air |url=https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/environmental-control/appendix-b-air.html |website=Centers for Disease Control and Prevention |date=2024-01-11 |at=Airborne Contaminant Removal}}</ref>


For t = 1h and ACH = 1 we get: <math>\frac{C(1)}{C_0}=\text{ exp( }-\text{1 }*\text{  }1) \approx 0.368</math>

It means that 36.8 % of the initial pollutant concentration remains after 1 hour at 1 ACH. It corresponds to a 63.2 % concentration reduction of the pollutant.

In order to achieve [[wikt:equilibrium|equilibrium]] pressure, the amount of return air (air leaving the space) and the amount of supply air (air entering the space) must be the same.

== Definitions ==
{{Glossary}}
{{term|Age of air}}
{{defn|The average time elapsed since molecules of air in a given volume of air entered the building from outside.}}
{{term|Concentration}}
{{defn|The quantity of one constituent dispersed in a defined amount of another.}}
{{term|Concentration, tracer gas}}
{{defn|The volume or mass of tracer gas divided by the volume or mass of air plus tracer gas.}}
{{term|Outdoor air}}
{{defn|Air outside a building or taken from outdoors and not previously circulated through the system.}}
{{term|Perfect mixing}}
{{defn|A theoretical airflow distribution pattern within a ventilated space where the supply air is instantaneously and uniformly mixed with the air in the space such that the concentration of all constituents in the air, and the age of air, are spatially uniform.}}
{{term|Return air}}
{{defn|Air extracted from a space and totally or partially returned to an air conditioner, furnace, or other heat source.}}
{{term|Supply air}}
{{defn|Air entering a space from an air-conditioning, heating, or ventilating apparatus.}}
{{glossary end}}

==Formulas==
===Air changes per hour===
'''In Imperial units:'''
<math>\quad ACPH = \frac{60\text{ min }\cdot Q}{V}</math>

where:
*''ACPH'' = number of air changes per hour; higher values correspond to more ventilation
*''Q'' = Volumetric flow rate of air in cubic feet per minute (cfm)
*''V'' = Space [[volume]] ''L'' × ''W'' × ''H'', in cubic feet

'''In metric units'''
<math> \quad ACPH = \frac{3600\text{ s }\cdot Q}{V} </math>

where:
*''ACPH'' = number of air changes per hour; higher values correspond to more ventilation
*''Q'' = Volumetric flow rate of air in cubic meters per second (m<sup>3</sup>/s)
*''V'' = Space [[volume]] ''L'' × ''W'' × ''H'', in cubic meters

For a given room or building size and number of air changes per hour, the volumetric flow requirement is usually specified in [[cubic meters per hour]] when using metric units.<ref>[https://www.dibk.no/regelverk/byggteknisk-forskrift-tek17/13/i/13-2 § 13-2. Ventilasjon i boligbygning - Direktoratet for byggkvalitet]</ref>

===Ventilation rates===
Ventilation rates are often expressed as a volume rate per person (CFM per person, L/s per person). The conversion between air changes per hour and ventilation rate per person is as follows:

<math> \quad R_p = \frac{ACPH*D*h}{60} </math>

where:
*''R<sub>p</sub>'' = ventilation rate per person (in cubic feet per minute per person (cfm/person))
*''ACPH'' = Air changes per hour
*''D'' = floor area per occupant (in square feet per occupant)
*''h'' = Ceiling height (in feet)

Having <math>1 m^3/h = 
{1,000 \over 3,600} L/s = {1 \over 3.6} L/s</math>, the corresponding metric expression for liters per second per person is:

<math> \quad R_p = \frac{ACPH*D*h}{3.6} </math>

where:
*''R<sub>p</sub>'' = ventilation rate per person (in liters per second per person)
*''ACPH'' = Air changes per hour
*''D'' = floor area per person (in square meters per person)
*''h'' = Ceiling height (in metesr)

==Air change rate recommendations==
Air change rates are often used as [[rules of thumb]] in ventilation design. However, they are seldom used as the actual basis of design or calculation. For example, residential ventilation rates are calculated based on area of the residence and number of occupants.<ref name="ASHRAE 62.2">{{cite book |year=2022 |title=ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 62.2-2022: Ventilation and Acceptable Indoor Air Quality in Low-Rise Residential Buildings |journal= |location=Atlanta, GA |publisher=American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers |pages=58 |issn=1041-2336}}</ref> Non-residential ventilation rates are based on floor area and number of occupants, or a calculated dilution of known contaminants.<ref name="ASHRAE 62.1">{{cite book |year=2022 |title=ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 62.1-2022: Ventilation and Acceptable Indoor Air Quality |journal= |location=Atlanta, GA |publisher=American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers |pages=90 |issn=1041-2336}}</ref>  Hospital design standards use air changes per hour.<ref name="ASHRAE 170">{{cite book |year=2021 |title=ANSI/ASHRAE/ASHE Standard 170-2021: Ventilation of Health Care Facilities |journal= |location=Atlanta, GA |publisher=American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers |pages=54 |issn=1041-2336}}</ref> Recommended air changes rates can be found in relevant standards.<ref name="ASHRAE 62.2" /><ref name="ASHRAE 62.1" /><ref name="ASHRAE 170" /> Recent research indicates that Air Changes per Hour (ACH) alone may not be a reliable parameter for making ventilation recommendations. A new parameter, ''effective'' Air Changes per Hour (called ACHH by Mojtaba Zabihi et al.<ref name="link.springer.com">{{cite journal |last1=Zabihi |first1=Mojtaba |last2=Li |first2=Ri |last3=Brinkerhoff |first3=Joshua |title=Influence of indoor airflow on airborne disease transmission in a classroom |journal=Building Simulation |date=1 March 2024 |volume=17 |issue=3 |pages=355–370 |doi=10.1007/s12273-023-1097-y |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12273-023-1097-y |language=en |issn=1996-8744|url-access=subscription }}</ref>), which incorporates both the flow rate and large-scale airflow patterns, could provide a more accurate measure of how efficiently air is supplied and circulated within a room. This is particularly important for effectively managing airborne disease spread.<ref name="link.springer.com"/>

Filtration contributes to airborne contaminant removal, we introduce the notion of equivalent air changes per hour to express the contribution of these air-cleaning technologies. For a portable air cleaner we have:<ref>{{Cite web |last=CDC |date=2026-10-28 |title=How Much Ventilation Is Enough? |url=https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/ventilation/prevention/Aim-for-5.html |access-date=2026-11-06 |website=Ventilation |language=en-us}}</ref>

<math> eACH = \frac{CADR}{V}  </math>

where:

*eACH = equivalent clean-air delivery (resulting from filtration or other air treatment) (in number of air exchanges per hour)
*CADR = clean air delivery rate (characterizing the particle-removal performance of air cleaners) (in cubic meter per hour)
*V = space volume (in cubic meter)

The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]] (CDC) recommends aiming for at least five ACH of clean air, when feasible, in order to reduce airborne viral particles, while the [[EPA]] mentions that particle filtration can't be used as an alternative of outdoor-air ventilation systems.<ref>{{Cite web |last=CDC |date=2026-10-28 |title=How Much Ventilation Is Enough? |url=https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/ventilation/prevention/Aim-for-5.html |access-date=2026-11-06 |website=Ventilation |language=en-us}}</ref> The five ACH target from CDC is not a universal requirement as ventilation depends on many factors such as space, occupancy and intended use.

== Methods of measurement ==
Air changes per hour is a measurement intended to communicate the air change effectiveness of a space's ventilation system. Discussion around the ASHRAE standard 62, Ventilation for Acceptable Indoor Air Quality led to the development of a more direct method of measuring air change effectiveness with the use of a tracer gas.<ref name=":2" /> A tracer gas is a small amount of easily detected gas which is mixed with air in order to study airflow patterns.
This method directly compares the age of the air where occupants breathe to the age of air that would occur were the air of the space perfectly mixed. The method is designed to more accurately understand the effects of air-flow patterns within a space, to identify or avoid such occurrences as short-circuiting airflow patterns, in which most of the supply air goes directly to the exhaust, and fails to mix with the air already present.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" />

There are two ways to apply this method; the most commonly used technique, Tracer Gas Decay (step-down), consists of a short burst of gas injected into the space to establish a constant concentration within the building, then injection is stopped and concentration decay at a certain position is recorded, and second Tracer Gas Step-Up, where tracer gas is injected at a constant rate and the concentration response at a certain position is recorded<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Van Buggenhout |first1=S. |last2=Van Brecht |first2=A. |last3=Eren Özcan |first3=S. |last4=Vranken |first4=E. |last5=Van Malcot |first5=W. |last6=Berckmans |first6=D. |title=Influence of sampling positions on accuracy of tracer gas measurements in ventilated spaces |journal=Biosystems Engineering |date=October 2009 |volume=104 |issue=2 |pages=216–223 |doi=10.1016/j.biosystemseng.2009.04.018 |bibcode=2009BiSyE.104..216V }}</ref>

== Airtightness in building ==
The most common technique to measure [[Building airtightness|airtightness]] is the fan pressurization method, also known as the [[Blower door|blower door test]] at 50 Pa. It is measured by the number of air changes per hour (ACH) that occur when there is a differential pressure of 50 pascals between outside and inside the building. Thus the ACH measured under these conditions is qualified as ACH50. If an air volume equal to the inside volume of the building flows across the envelope in one hour, then ACH = 1.<ref>{{Citation |last=Jelley |first=Nick |chapter=airtightness |date=2017-01-19 |chapter-url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/view/10.1093/acref/9780191826276.001.0001/acref-9780191826276-e-20 |title=A Dictionary of Energy Science |publisher=Oxford University Press |language=en |isbn=978-0-19-182627-6 |access-date=2022-11-16}}</ref> Airtightness improves buildings' energy performance since low airtightness levels imply high [[Infiltration (HVAC)|infiltration]] rates, draughts, risk of condensation, and moisture accumulation, and other effects.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gillott |first1=M.C. |last2=Loveday |first2=D.L. |last3=White |first3=J. |last4=Wood |first4=C.J. |last5=Chmutina |first5=K. |last6=Vadodaria |first6=K. |title=Improving the airtightness in an existing UK dwelling: The challenges, the measures and their effectiveness |journal=Building and Environment |date=January 2016 |volume=95 |pages=227–239 |doi=10.1016/j.buildenv.2015.08.017 |bibcode=2016BuEnv..95..227G |s2cid=56109406 |url=https://figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/9451430 }}</ref> For this reason, the [[Passive House]] standard established performance requirements for airtightness requiring be less than 0.6 ACH with a pressure difference between inside and outside of 50 Pa.<ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-69938-7 |title=Building a Passive House |series=Green Energy and Technology |year=2018 |isbn=978-3-319-69937-0 }}</ref>

It is worth noting that ACH measured with the blower door test, at a differential pressure of 50 pascals, mimics the situation of a sustained 20 mph (32 km/h) wind outside. The natural air leakage, under calmer conditions, is likely to be much less. As a result, the so-called natural ACH may be a factor of 10-25 times smaller (approximation, can't be applied universally).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Randy |title=Measuring Naturial Air Leakage |url=https://building-performance.org/bpa-journal/ach50-achnat/ |website=BPA Journal |publisher=Building Performance Association |access-date=24 January 2025 |date=15 May 2023}}</ref> This is of relevance since high-performance building methodologies strive to keep ACH low under standardized, weather-stressed conditions, while air quality considerations may require sufficiently high natural ACH.

== Effects of ACH due to forced ventilation in a dwelling ==
Forced ventilation to increase ACH becomes a necessity to maintain acceptable air quality as occupants become reluctant to open windows due to behavioural changes such as keeping windows closed for security.<ref name=":0">Pollard, AR and McNeil, S, ''Forced Air Ventilation Systems'', June 2010, Report IEQ7570/3 for Beacon Pathway Limited</ref>

Air changes are often cited as a means of preventing condensation in houses with forced ventilation systems often rated 3–5 ACH though without referencing the size of the house. However, where ACH is already greater than 0.75 a forced ventilation system is unlikely to be of use at controlling condensation and instead insulation or heating are better remedies.<ref name=":0" /> Seven out of eight houses studied in NZ in 2010 had an ACH (corrected for ventilation factors) of 0.75 or greater.<ref name=":0" /> The presence of forced ventilation systems has been shown in some cases to actually increase the humidity rather than lower it.<ref name=":0" /> By displacing air inside a dwelling with infiltrated air (air brought in from outside the dwelling), positive pressure ventilation systems can increase heating (in winter) or cooling (in summer) requirements in a house.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">Warren Fitzgerald, Dr Inga Smith and Muthasim Fahmy, ''Heating and cooling potential of roof space air: implications for ventilation systems'', May 2011, Prepared for the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Authority (EECA)</ref> For example, to maintain a 15 °C temperature in a certain dwelling about 3.0 kW of heating are required at 0 ACH (no heat loss due to warmed air leaving the dwelling, instead heat is lost due to conduction or radiation), 3.8 kW at 1 ACH and 4.5 kW are required at 2 ACH.<ref name=":0" /> The use of roof space for heating or cooling was seen as ineffectual with the maximum heating benefits occurring in winter in more southerly regions (being close to the South Pole in these southern hemisphere reports) but being equivalent only to about 0.5 kW or the heating provided by about five 100 W incandescent light bulbs; cooling effects in summer were similarly small and were more pronounced for more northerly homes (being closer to the equator); in all cases the values assumed that the ventilation system automatically disengaged when the infiltrating air was warmer or cooler (as appropriate) than the air already in the dwelling as it would otherwise exacerbate the undesirable conditions in the house.<ref name=":1" />

'''''Cyclophora albiocellaria''''' is a [[moth]] of the family [[Geometridae]]. It is found in south-eastern [[Europe]] and parts of Central-[[Asia]].

The [[wingspan]] is 20–25 mm in the first generation and only about 18 mm in the second generation. The apex of the forewing is slightly pointed. The ground colour is pale yellow with an orange tinge. The postmedial line is dissolved to brown dots. The medial area towards postmedial line and towards the inner area shows a strong black brown coloration on all wings. Cell rings are large and round on all wings with a white centre.

(MHNT) Cyclophora albiocellaria - Gruszowa Poland - Male dorsal.jpg|♂

</gallery>
The [[larva]]e feed on ''[[Acer campestre]]''.

==Taxonomy==
''[[Cyclophora lennigiaria]]'' is treated as a subspecies of ''Cyclophora albiocellaria'' by some authors.

The '''1887 San Diego mayoral election''' was held on November 8, 1887, to elect the [[Mayor of San Diego|mayor]] for [[San Diego]]. This was the first mayoral election since the position was abolished due to an 1852 city bankruptcy. [[William Jefferson Hunsaker]] was elected Mayor with a majority of the votes.

==Candidates==
*[[William Jefferson Hunsaker]], lawyer<ref name=elections>{{cite news|last1=Larson|first1=Thomas|title=Elections San Diego Style|url=http://www.sandiegoreader.com/news/2004/oct/28/elections-san-diego-style/|access-date=March 16, 2017|work=San Diego Reader|date=October 28, 2004|language=en}}</ref>
*[[Daniel C. Reed]], insurance salesman<ref name="elections" />

==Campaign==
In 1887, the City of San Diego adopted a new charter reestablishing the office of mayor for the first time in 35 years since an 1852 city bankruptcy. In the interim, the city had been run by a board of trustees appointed by the State.<ref name="elections" />

On October 4, 1887, trade unions of San Diego met to nominate a slate of candidates to run for office on the platform of the [[Workingmen's Party of California]]. On the fourth ballot, [[William Jefferson Hunsaker|William J. Hunsaker]] was selected as the Workingmen's candidate for mayor.<ref>{{cite news|title=The Labor Ticket|url=http://infoweb.newsbank.com/resources/doc/nb/image/v2:136E6A0F0DF56B38@EANX-13ED00166326F00C@2410549-13ECAEB73395EEBD@2-13ED75A9D5AF9320@?p=WORLDNEWS|access-date=March 16, 2017|work=The San Diego Union|date=October 4, 1887}}</ref> His opponent, [[Daniel C. Reed]] ran as a [[Republican Party (US)|Republican]] on the Citizen's ticket.<ref>{{cite news|title=Our Candidates|url=http://infoweb.newsbank.com/resources/doc/nb/image/v2:136E6A0F0DF56B38@EANX-13ED0025661F878B@2410564-13ECB18039D3935F@4-13ED779041B5BA98@?p=WORLDNEWS|access-date=March 16, 2017|work=The San Diego Union|date=October 19, 1887}}</ref>

On November 8, 1887, Hunsaker was elected mayor with 53.8 percent of the vote to Reed's 46.2 percent.<ref name="results" />

'''''68 Kill''''' is a 2017 American [[black comedy]] [[Crime film|crime thriller]] directed and written by [[Trent Haaga]] and starring [[Matthew Gray Gubler]], [[AnnaLynne McCord]], [[Alisha Boe]], [[Sheila Vand]], Sam Eidson and Michael Beasley. It is based on the Bryan Smith novel of the same name. The film was released on August 4, 2017, by [[Independent Film Company|IFC Midnight]]. It made an estimated $96,343 in total domestic video sales.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/68-Kill#tab=summary|title = 68 Kill (2017) - Financial Information}}</ref>

==Plot==
Chip is a timid sewer worker who is at the beck and call of his bombshell girlfriend. Liza is unhappy with her life as a prostitute and she is repeatedly abusive towards Chip in their relationship, but he is convinced that he is in love with her. One day, Liza's landlord and steady client, Ken McKenzie, shows her a safe that contains $68,000. She convinces Chip to steal the $68,000 with her. The two sneak into the McKenzies' house, armed and masked. Chip's apprehension of the mission is increased when he sees Liza kill the McKenzies, who witnessed the two burglars in the house. During their heist, a young woman named Violet sees Chip with the McKenzies' bodies and flees. Liza knocks Violet out cold and plans to sell her to her brother Dwayne, who will presumably torture and kill Violet.

Disgusted by Liza's plan, Chip knocks out Liza when she goes to get Violet from the trunk of their car. He shoots at a bypasser who tries to intervene in the situation; when Dwayne emerges from the building waving a machete, Chip shoots him in the shoulder. He then drives away with the money. Liza regains consciousness and chases after Chip, getting him to pull over. She tells him that she forgives him as long as he stays with her, but then loses consciousness again on the side of the road. Chip leaves her there and keeps driving away, until he hears Violet's voice from the trunk and remembers his hostage. When he goes to release her, she subdues him and holds him at gunpoint. With no other option, he decides to take Violet with him to flee with the money. Both are attracted to the other, as they bond over music and jokes in the car. On their trip, a police officer pulls them over, but Violet manages to talk their way out of the policeman inspecting the car further. Chip is impressed at her quick thinking, and the two further bond.

They stop at a gas station, where the clerk, Monica, sees Chip pull out a $100 bill from the envelope of the stolen money. She convinces him to give her more money for her to keep quiet, but Violet steps in and refuses for Chip. The two spend the night at a nearby hotel, where Violet tearfully explains that she was at the McKenzies' that night because McKenzie was forcing her to have sex with him for money. The two make love that night, seemingly safe.

The morning after, Chip wakes up to find his gun, money, and clothes stolen. Frantic, he is mad at himself for letting his guard down around Violet, who he assumes stole his possessions. He discovers her dead body in the bathtub of the room, horrified. Chip asks the man working at the hotel to use his phone to call Liza, since he thinks she is the one behind Violet's murder. The man working tells Chip a description of one of the people at his room the night before, which Chip connects to the gas station worker, Monica. Chip reluctantly incapacitates the man, finds some clothes from the lost-and-found, and steals his car. He goes to the gas station, where the employee working tells Chip where Monica is, with Chip reluctantly giving her [[cunnilingus]] in return.

When Chip arrives at the house, it is revealed he has been set up, as the employee was a friend of Monica's. He is taken inside, where one of the men in the house holds him at gunpoint. Chip tries to escape, but is knocked unconscious. Monica explains how and why she robbed Chip and framed him for Violet's death, even though her plan has many faults in it. Monica's group beats Chip while taking drugs that they bought with the stolen money. Chip eventually loses consciousness and has a vision of Violet, who tells him to wake up. When he does, he finds Liza is there, with a gun pointed at his face. Monica and one of her cohorts come out from the bedroom, and threaten Liza. Suddenly, Liza's brother (Dwayne) enters the room, and kills almost all of Monica's gang. With Liza and her brother now in control of the situation, Dwayne orders the two surviving members of Monica's gang (Monica and another woman) into the bedroom, where he rapes and kills one of them, leaving Monica as the only survivor from her original gang. Liza tells Chip that all is forgiven, as long as he still acts as her dog. He refuses, shoots and kills her, then goes into the bedroom to kill Dwayne. Monica thanks Chip for saving her from Dwayne "the pervert," and tells him that she will do anything that he wants her to do. He informs her that he wants her to bring the deceased Violet back to life, and then shoots and kills her (to avenge Monica's murdering of Violet in the first place.) Chip stages the scene to erase his presence at the house, takes the money, and escapes as the cops are driving in the direction of the murder house. On the side of the road, Chip spots a beautiful but provocatively tattooed woman with her car broken down. He considers picking her up, but ultimately speeds far away from her, content with his independence and the money.
